newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called mostly higher, cash holds.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called mostly higher, cash holds.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open mostly higher Tuesday as cash was talked little changed and cool weather continued across the Northeast and Midwest, market sources said.
July over-the-counter trade bounced back and forth between $2.15 and $2.17 at 0935 EDT after settling to the downside Monday at $2.147 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, July last traded 0.2 cent lower at $2.145.
Early cash prices at Henry Hub were talked at $2.19-2.21 per mmBtu.
Technically, traders said July resistance was at $2.21 and then at $2.25 and $2.37. Support was pegged at last week's low of $2.055 and then at $2.

In Monday's cash, Louisiana Gulf Coast gas firmed about four cents to the mid-to-high teens. Midcon pipes gained a similar amount to about $2.02-2.03. New York city gate gas also was about five cents firmer at $2.40-2.45.

Near- to slightly below-normal temperatures forecast throughout most of the Northeast and Midwest will likely temper demand this week, traders said, but patches of heat in the Southwest will continue to attract those buyers to the market.
Separately, injection estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report have ranged from 78 to 110 bcf, versus a gain of 87 bcf a year ago.
